To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) contrastive learning of video representations can be used for learning generalizable global-local representations that can be used for various downstream scenarios; (2) the global and local contrastive learning tasks are complementary and can be used to learn representations for both global and local tasks; (3) contrastive learning can be used to train video models with limited labeled data, which is useful for many applications such as event localization and deepfake detection.
we propose a contrastive learning framework to learn global-local representations from videos and audios, and that the learned representations are more generalizable to different downstream tasks.
